findings: The preserved source requires DFS and asks only for the maximum average value among binary-tree subtrees; it does not preserve a concrete API, empty-tree behavior, node range or tie rule.
The candidate explicitly defines subtree as each node plus all descendants and labels return/null/numeric-range behavior as answer-side rather than recovered source.
The postorder invariant is correct: left and right sum/count plus the current node produce exactly the current rooted subtree statistics, so each candidate is evaluated once in O(n) time.
All-negative input is handled without a synthetic zero baseline; the first real subtree initializes the best fraction.

Best-fraction comparisons use BigInteger cross products, avoiding both floating selection error and overflow in long cross multiplication, while Math.addExact makes the declared long-sum boundary observable.

The writer harness matches an independent repeated-subtree oracle on 3000 generated trees; a separately authored reviewer harness matches on 5000 additional trees and explicit negative/fraction boundaries.
The answer calls out O(h) recursion depth and does not invent project experience.
